question_text: In ΔPQR, right angled at Q, PR + QR = 25 cm and PQ = 5 cm. Determine the values of sin P, cos P and tan P.

question_image.description: Diagram of triangle PQR with right angle at Q.

answer_text: PR = 13 cm, QR = 12 cm. Therefore, sin P = \frac{QR}{PR} = \frac{12}{13}, cos P = \frac{PQ}{PR} = \frac{5}{13}, tan P = \frac{QR}{PQ} = \frac{12}{5}.
answer_latex: PR = 13 \text{ cm}, QR = 12 \text{ cm}. \text{ Therefore, } sin P = \frac{QR}{PR} = \frac{12}{13}, cos P = \frac{PQ}{PR} = \frac{5}{13}, tan P = \frac{QR}{PQ} = \frac{12}{5}.

steps.description: Let PR be x, then QR = 25 - x.
Apply Pythagoras theorem: x^2 = 5^2 + (25 - x)^2.
Solve for x to find PR.
Calculate QR using QR = 25 - PR.
Calculate sin P, cos P, and tan P.
steps.expression: sin P = \frac{12}{13}, cos P = \frac{5}{13}, tan P = \frac{12}{5}

final_answer: Thus, sin P = \frac{12}{13}, cos P = \frac{5}{13}, tan P = \frac{12}{5}.
